nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِي أَنْزَلَ عَلَىٰ عَبْدِهِ ٱلْكِتَابَ وَلَمْ يَجْعَل لَّهُ عِوَجَا. قَيِّمَاً﴾.
There are two views on this:
The first: that it involves taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr (fronting and postponement).
The meaning is: Praise be to Allah, who sent down upon His servant the Book upright (قيِّماً), and did not make for it any crookedness (عِوَجاً).
This meaning is related from Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Bakr ibn Sahl narrated to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us; he said: Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us; he said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated to me from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَلَمْ يَجْعَل لَّهُ عِوَجَا. قَيِّمَاً﴾ — he says: He sent down the Book just and upright, and did not make it crooked or confused.
The other view: Saʿīd related it from Qatāda, who said: In one of the readings: "الحمدُ لله الذي أنزل عبده الكتاب ولم يجعل له عِوَجَاً، ولكنْ جعله قيِّماً" ("Praise be to Allah who sent down [to] His servant the Book and did not make for it any crookedness, but made it upright").
[Translator's note: the quoted reading appears in the source as «أنزل عبده» without «على»; it is translated as written.]
On the saying of the Exalted ﴿وَلَمْ يَجْعَل لَّهُ عِوَجَا﴾ there are two views:
The first: that He did not make it inconsistent, as He, Glorified is He, said: ﴿وَلَوْ كَانَ مِنْ عِنْدِ غَيْرِ اللَّهِ لَوَجَدُوا فِيهِ اخْتِلافَاً كَثِيراً﴾.
The other view: that He did not make it created, as is related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said concerning the saying of the Exalted ﴿قُرْآناً عَرَبِيَّاً غَيْرَ ذِي عِوَجٍ﴾: not created.
And on His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿قَيِّمَاً﴾ there are two views:
The first: Juwaybir related it from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: straight.
The other view: that it is a guardian (قيِّماً) over the [previous] Books, i.e. it confirms them.

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿لِّيُنْذِرَ بَأْساً شَدِيداً مِّن لَّدُنْهُُ﴾.
The meaning is: to warn you of a severe punishment, just as the Exalted said: ﴿إنَّما ذَلكُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ يُخَوِّفُ أَوْ لِيَاءَهُ﴾ [i.e. frightens you with his allies].

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿كَبُرَتْ كَلِمَةً تَخْرُجُ مِنْ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ إِن يَقُولُونَ إِلاَّ كَذِباًً﴾.
The meaning is: That word is grievous as a word (كلمةً) in Allah's sight — and it is their saying ﴿اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَداً﴾ — i.e. grievous as a word.
It is also said: It carries the sense of taʿajjub (wonder), as one says of a judge who judged with the truth: «ما أقضاه» ("How [excellent a] judge he is!").
So the meaning would be: What a grievous word it is!
Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar read ﴿كَبُرَتْ كَلِمَةٌ تَخْرُجُ مِنْ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ﴾ with the nominative.
Its meaning is: it became great (grave). One says «كَبُرَ الشيءُ» when a thing becomes great, and «كَبِرَ» when someone grows old.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَعَلَّكَ بَاخِعٌ نَّفْسَكَ عَلَىٰ آثَارِهِمْ﴾.
Saʿīd related from Qatāda that he said: [باخع means] killing yourself. Then He said: ﴿عَلَىٰ آثَارِهِمْ﴾, i.e. after them.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إِن لَّمْ يُؤْمِنُواْ بِهَـٰذَا ٱلْحَدِيثِ أَسَفاً﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, in anger.
Mujāhid said: That is, in anguish.
And this is closer, i.e. out of grief for them.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا مَا عَلَى ٱلأَرْضِ زِينَةً لَّهَا﴾.
Quṭrub said: That is, whatever is on the earth by which it is adorned.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿لِنَبْلُوَهُمْ أَيُّهُم أَحْسَنُ عَمَلاً﴾.
That is, so that We may test them.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنَّا لَجَاعِلُونَ مَا عَلَيْهَا صَعِيداً جُرُزاًً﴾.
Saʿīd related from Qatāda that he said: That is, with no trees on it, no vegetation and no building.
Mujāhid said: That is, a barren waste (بَلْقَعاً).
Abū Jaʿfar said: «الصعيد» in the language is the face of the earth, and from this soil is called «صعيد».
And «الجُرُز» in the language is land on which there is no vegetation.
Al-Kisāʾī said: One says «جَرُزَتِ الأرضُ تَجْرُزُ» (the land became bare), and «جَرزَهَا القومُ يَجْرِزُونَها» when people have eaten all the vegetation and crops on it; so it is «مَجْروزة» and «جُرُز».

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمْ حَسِبْتَ أَنَّ أَصْحَابَ ٱلْكَهْفِ وَٱلرَّقِيمِ كَانُواْ مِنْ آيَاتِنَا عَجَباًً﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿الكهفُ﴾ is the cave in the valley, and ﴿الرَّقيمُ﴾ is the valley.
Yazīd ibn Dirham said: Anas ibn Mālik was asked about the Cave and al-Raqīm, and he said: ﴿الكهفُ﴾ is the mountain, ﴿والرَّقيمُ﴾ is the dog.
Sufyān ibn Saʿīd related from Simāk, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he asked Kaʿb: What is al-Raqīm? He said: It is the name of the town from which they went out.
ʿIkrima said: ﴿الرَّقيمُ﴾ is the inkwell.
Mujāhid said: ﴿الرَّقيمُ﴾ is the writing (the book).
Al-Suddī said: the rock.
Al-Farrāʾ said: al-Raqīm is a tablet of lead on which were written their names, their lineages, their religion, and from whom they fled.
Abū ʿUbayda said: al-Raqīm is [the valley] in which the cave is.
Isrāʾīl related from Simāk, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "I know all of the Qurʾān except four: غِسْلِين, حَنَان, الأَوَّاه and الرَّقيم."
Sufyān ibn Ḥusayn related from Yaʿlā ibn Muslim, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he mentioned the Companions of the Cave and said: "The young men went missing; their families searched for them but did not find them. The matter was raised to the king, who said: 'There will surely be some news of them.' He had a tablet of lead brought, wrote their names on it and placed it in his treasuries. That tablet is al-Raqīm."
Wakīʿ related from Abū Makīn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: al-Raqīm is "a tablet [on which are the names of young men whose names were inscribed in the rock; that is the writing]."
In some narrations: their names and their story were written on a tablet, and it was placed at the entrance of the cave.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The narrations related from Ibn ʿAbbās are not contradictory,
because he only heard the first view from Kaʿb,
and as for the second view, it may be that he came to know [what] al-Raqīm [is] after that.
The best that has been said about it is that it is the writing, and that is well known in the language: one says «رقمتُ الشيءَ», i.e. I wrote it. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿كِتَابٌ مَرْقُومٌ﴾.
And ﴿رقيمٌ﴾ has the sense of «مرقوم» (inscribed), just as one says «قتيل» in the sense of «مقتول» (killed).
Ibn Jurayj related from Mujāhid on the saying of the Exalted ﴿كَانُواْ مِنْ آيَاتِنَا عَجَباً﴾ that he said: They are a wonder.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Mujāhid takes the view that it is not a rebuke to the Prophet ﷺ for holding them to be a wonder.
But Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid that he said: He is saying: They are not the most wondrous of Our signs.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذْ أَوَى ٱلْفِتْيَةُ إِلَى ٱلْكَهْفِ فَقَالُواْ رَبَّنَآ آتِنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحْمَةً وَهَيِّىءْ لَنَا مِنْ أَمْرِنَا رَشَداً﴾.
That is, guide us to the things most beloved to You.

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَضَرَبْنَا عَلَىٰ آذَانِهِمْ فِي ٱلْكَهْفِ سِنِينَ عَدَداً﴾.
That is, We prevented them from hearing; and the meaning is: We put them to sleep, because if they had heard they would have woken. Then He said ﴿سِنِينَ عَدَدَاً﴾.
On the benefit of His saying ﴿عَدَدَاً﴾ there are two views:
The first: that it is [tawkīd (emphasis) and singles out [the number] from the unit.
The other: that it is emphasis of the sense of multitude], because a small number does not need counting, since it is already known.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ بَعَثْنَاهُمْ﴾.
That is, from their sleep. Whoever is brought back to life, or roused from his sleep, is called «مبعوث» (raised), because he had been prevented from rising and moving about.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿لِنَعْلَمَ أَيُّ الحِزْبَيْنِ أَحْصَىٰ لِمَا لَبِثُواْ أَمَداً﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, in number.
Abū Jaʿfar said: «الأمد» in the language is the limit (the extent).

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَرَبَطْنَا عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْْ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, with faith.
The meaning according to the lexicographers is: We gave them patience and made them firm.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إِذْ قَامُواْ فَقَالُواْ رَبُّنَا رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ لَن نَّدْعُوَاْ مِن دُونِهِ إِلـٰهاً﴾.
So they rejected that anything other than Allah be worshipped alongside Him.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿لَّقَدْ قُلْنَا إِذاً شَطَطاً﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, a lie.
Abū Jaʿfar said: «الشطط» in the language is going beyond bounds in injustice.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ قَوْمُنَا ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِهِ آلِهَةً لَّوْلاَ يَأْتُونَ عَلَيْهِم بِسُلْطَانٍ بَيِّنٍٍ﴾.
Ibn ʿUyayna related from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās: "Every «سلطان» in the Qurʾān means a proof."

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذِ ٱعْتَزَلْتُمُوهُمْ وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ إِلاَّ ٱللَّهَ﴾.
The meaning is: You have withdrawn from what they worship, except Allah, for you have not abandoned His worship.
Saʿīd related from Qatāda that he said: In the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: ﴿وَإِذِ اعْتَزَلْتُمُوهُمْ وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ ("…and what they worship besides Allah").
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَأْوُوا إِلَى ٱلْكَهْفِ﴾.
That is, make it your refuge.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿يَنْشُرْ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُم مِّن رَّحْمَتِهِ وَيُهَيِّئْ لَكُمْ مِّنْ أَمْرِكُمْ مِّرْفَقاً﴾.
[It has been read with a fatḥa and with a kasra on the mīm, and it is that which one makes use of (relies on); likewise «مِرْفَق» and «مَرْفِق» of a person (the elbow). Some make «المَرْفِق», with a fatḥa on the mīm and a kasra on the fāʾ, [belong to] matters (affairs), and «المُرْفق» [sic] [belong to] the human being. It has also been said: «المَرْفِق» with a fatḥa on the mīm is the place, like «المسجد». They are two dialectal forms.]
[Translator's note: «المُرْفق» is vowelled with a ḍamma in the source, which conflicts with the preceding description; translated as written.]

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَقْولَنَّ لِشَيْءٍ إِنِّي فَاعِلٌ ذٰلِكَ غَداً إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
[It is related that the Prophet ﷺ was asked about] young men who had passed away in former times, about a man who travelled widely, and about the spirit. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Tomorrow I will tell you about that," and he did not make the exception [by saying "if Allah wills"]. So Gabriel stayed away from him for some ten-odd nights, then came to him with Sūrat al-Kahf, and concerning his saying "I will tell you about it tomorrow" there was revealed: ﴿وَلاَ تَقْولَنَّ لِشَيْءٍ إِنِّي فَاعِلٌ ذٰلِكَ غَداً إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَقُلْ عَسَىٰ أَن يَهْدِيَنِ رَبِّي لأَقْرَبَ مِنْ هَـٰذَا رَشَداًً﴾.
That is, perhaps He will give me signs and proofs that are more guiding and clearer than the story of the Companions of the Cave.

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلَبِثُواْ فِي كَهْفِهِمْ ثَلاثَ مِئَةٍ سِنِينَ وَٱزْدَادُواْ تِسْعاً﴾.
There are three views on its meaning:
a. Mujāhid said: This is the number [of years] they remained.
b. Qatāda said: In the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: "وَقَالُوا لَبِثُوا في كَهْفِهمْ" ("And they said: they remained in their cave…").
c. The third view: that Allah has reported how long they remained until they were raised from the cave, and we do not know how long it has been from the time they were raised until this time; so He, Glorified is He, said ﴿قُل اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا لَبِثُوا﴾, i.e. from the time of their raising until this time.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The best of these views is the first. The difficulty in it arises only because of His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا لَبِثُوا﴾; so some people took refuge in saying: it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the saying of the Exalted ﴿سَيقُولُونَ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: We chose the first view only because it is more eloquent, and because Ibn Fuḍayl related from al-Ajlaḥ, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: When ﴿وَلَبِثُواْ فِي كَهْفِهِمْ ثَلاثَ مِئَةٍ﴾ was sent down, they said: "Years? Or months? Or days?" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down ﴿سِنِينَ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: As for what is difficult in the saying of the Exalted ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ أعلمُ بِمَا لَبِثُوا﴾, we shall explain it.
It may be that, since they disagreed over how long they had remained, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, then reported it and said: ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ أعْلَمُ بِمَا لَبِثُوا﴾, i.e. He knows it better than those who disagree about it.
Another view, better than this: that «أعلمُ» (more knowing) has the sense of «عالمٌ» (knowing). That is frequent and found in the speech of the Arabs. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَبْدَأُ الخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ وَهُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَيْهِ﴾ — the soundest view on it is that its meaning is "it is easy for Him", and that is the choice of Abū al-ʿAbbās [al-Mubarrad]. From this also is «اللهُ أكبرُ» in the sense of «كبير» (great), and from this is the saying of al-Farazdaq:
إنَّ الَّذِي سَمَكَ السَّمَاءَ بَنَى لَنَا * بَيْتَاً دَعَائِمُهُ أَعَزُّ وأَطْوَلُ
(He who raised up the sky built for us a house whose pillars are mighty and tall [lit. "mightier and taller"].)
And the saying of another:
أَصْبَحْتُ أمْنَحُكِ الصُّدُودَ وَإنَّنِي * ـ قَسَمَاً إليكِ ـ مع الصُّدُودِ لأَمْيَلُ
(I have come to offer you aloofness, yet — I swear to you — despite the aloofness I am surely inclined [lit. "more inclined"] towards you.)
And the saying of another:
لَعَمْرُكَ مَا أدْرِي وإنِّي لأَوْجَلُ * عَلَى أَيِّنَا تَعْدُو المَنِيَّةُ أوَّلُ
(By your life, I do not know — and I am indeed afraid [lit. "more afraid"] — upon which of us death will fall first.)

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَبْصِرْ بِهِ وَأَسْمِعْ﴾.
The meaning is: How well He sees and how well He hears! i.e. He knows the story of the Companions of the Cave and others.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿مَا لَهُم مِّن دُونِهِ مِن وَلِيٍّ وَلاَ يُشْرِكُ فِي حُكْمِهِ أَحَداً﴾.
Its parallel is the saying of the Exalted ﴿فَلاَ يُظْهِرُ عَلَى غَيْبِهِ أَحَدَاً. إِلاَّ مَنِ ارْتَضَى مِنْ رَسُولٍ﴾.
And whoever reads ﴿ولا تُشْرِكْ في حُكْمِهِ أَحَدَاً﴾, its meaning for him is: Do not ascribe to anyone that he knows the Unseen.

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَ مُبَدِّلَ لِكَلِمَاتِهِ وَلَن تَجِدَ مِن دُونِهِ مُلْتَحَداًً﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, a refuge, i.e. something that would protect you from Him, Mighty and Majestic is He.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is good linguistically. Its origin in the language is from «اللَّحد», which is from inclining; and «الملحد» is the one who inclines away from the truth and deviates from it. So when you «ألحدتَ» to something, you have inclined to it.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱصْبِرْ نَفْسَكَ مَعَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلْغَدَاةِ وَٱلْعَشِيِّ يُرِيدُونَ وجْهَهُ﴾
Ibn ʿAjlān related from Nāfiʿ from Ibn ʿUmar that he said: [It is] the prescribed prayer.
Mujāhid and Ibrāhīm said: The five prayers.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ تَعْدُ عَيْنَاكَ عَنْهُمْ تُرِيدُ زِينَةَ ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾.
That is, do not pass beyond them to the people of luxury.
It is related from al-Ḥasan that he read ﴿وَلاَ تُعَدِّ عَيْنَيْكَ عَنْهُمْ﴾, with a doubled dāl and the accusative.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ تُطِعْ مَنْ أَغْفَلْنَا قَلْبَهُ عَن ذِكْرِنَا وَٱتَّبَعَ هَوَاهُ وَكَانَ أَمْرُهُ فُرُطاً﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, in loss (wasted).
Abū Jaʿfar said: It has also been said: extravagance; and it has been said: regret.
These views are close to one another; it is from «الإفراط» in a thing, i.e. going beyond bounds in it.
What makes this clear is that Sufyān ibn Saʿīd said: He is ʿUyayna ibn Ḥiṣn.
And someone else said: He said: "I am the noblest of Muḍar and the most eminent of them."
This is overstepping itself.
Al-Farrāʾ said: ﴿فُرُطَاً﴾: neglected, in which obedience has been abandoned.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَقُلِ ٱلْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكُمْ﴾.
The meaning is: And say: what I have brought you is the truth from your Lord.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَمَن شَآءَ فَلْيُؤْمِن وَمَن شَآءَ فَلْيَكْفُرْ﴾.
This is by way of threat.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إِنَّا أَعْتَدْنَا لِلظَّالِمِينَ نَاراً﴾.
That is, We have made it for them as «عَتَاد» (provision); and «العَتَاد» is what is fixed and inseparable, and it is like «العُدَّة» (equipment).
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أَحَاطَ بِهِمْ سُرَادِقُهَا﴾.
«السُّرادق» in the language is anything that surrounds something.
It has been said: What is meant by it is the smoke that will surround the unbelievers on the Day of Resurrection, and it is what Allah mentioned in His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿انْطَلِقُوا إِلَى ظِلٍّ ذِي ثَلاَثِ شُعَبٍ﴾.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَإِن يَسْتَغِيثُواْ يُغَاثُواْ بِمَآءٍ كَٱلْمُهْلِ يَشْوِي ٱلْوجُوهَ﴾.
Hushaym related from ʿAwf from al-Ḥasan, who said: Some people came to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd to ask him about «المُهْل». He took some silver and melted it until it flowed, then they were permitted to enter, and he said to them: This is the closest thing to «المُهْل».
Isrāʾīl related from Simāk, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said:
«المُهْل» is the dregs of oil.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid, who said: «المُهْل» is pus and blood.
Abū Jaʿfar said: These views are close to one another. It is only what has settled and become still, and it is most often used for the dregs of oil, as Ibn ʿAbbās said.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿يَشْوِي ٱلْوجُوهَ بِئْسَ ٱلشَّرَابُ وَسَآءَتْ مُرْتَفَقاًً﴾.
The meaning is: and evil is the Fire as a «مرتفَق».
Mujāhid said: That is, as a gathering place.
Someone else said: That is, as a sitting place.
Abū Jaʿfar said: What is well known in the language is that «المرتفَق» is a place of reclining (leaning on the elbow), and the lexicographers recited:
إنِّي أَرِقْتُ فَبِتُّ اللَّيْلَ مُرتَفِقَاً * كَأَنَّ عَيْنيَ فِيهَا الصَّابُ مَذْبُوحُ
(I lay sleepless and spent the night leaning on my elbow, as if bitter aloe-sap had been crushed into my eye.)
Abū Jaʿfar said: Nor is it impossible that the meaning be: a place of reclining.

nahhas-meani:30-30.t:
And His saying, exalted be His mention: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ إِنَّا لاَ نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ مَنْ أَحْسَنَ عَمَلاً﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū ʿAbd Allāh Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī ibn Sahl narrated to us; he said: Muḥammad ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us; he said: Yaḥyā ibn al-Ḍurays narrated to us, from Zuhayr ibn Muʿāwiya, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib, who said: A Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the Farewell Pilgrimage — while the Prophet was standing at ʿArafāt on his reddish-white she-camel — and said: "I am a man seeking knowledge, so tell me about the saying of Allah ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ إِنَّا لاَ نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ مَنْ أَحْسَنَ عَمَلاً﴾." The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "O Bedouin, you are not far from them, nor are they far from you. These four who are standing with me — Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān and ʿAlī — so let your people know that this verse was revealed concerning these four."

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهِمُ ٱلأَنْهَارُُ﴾.
«العَدْن» is residence (abiding). Then He said: ﴿تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهِمُ ٱلأَنْهَارُ﴾, i.e. the water of the rivers.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيهَا مِنْ أَسَاوِرَ مِن ذَهَبٍ﴾.
«أساور» is the plural of «أسْوِرة», and «أسْوِرة» is the plural of «سِوار» (bracelet); one also says «سُوار».
Quṭrub reported that «أساور» is the plural of «إسوار».
That is not known.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَيَلْبَسُونَ ثِيَاباً خُضْراً مِّن سُنْدُسٍ وَإِسْتَبْرَقٍ﴾.
«السندس» is fine brocade, and «الاستبرق» is its thick kind.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿مُّتَّكِئِينَ فِيهَا عَلَى ٱلأَرَآئِكِ﴾.
These are couches within canopied bridal chambers.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿نِعْمَ ٱلثَّوَابُ وَحَسُنَتْ مُرْتَفَقاً﴾.
That is, excellent is Paradise as a place of reclining.

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱضْرِبْ لهُمْ مَّثَلاً رَّجُلَيْنِ جَعَلْنَا لأَحَدِهِمَا جَنَّتَيْنِ مِنْ أَعْنَابٍ﴾.
It is related that the Jews said: Ask him about the Companions of the Cave, about the spirit, and about two men. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent this down and made it a parable for all people.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَحَفَفْنَاهُمَا بِنَخْلٍ﴾.
That is, We surrounded them with it. One says «حفَّ القومُ بفلانٍ» when they encircle him.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا بَيْنَهُمَا زَرْعاً﴾.
So He reported that there was nothing between them but cultivated land.

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
Then He reported that both of them were at the utmost in yielding produce and fruit, and said: ﴿كِلْتَا ٱلْجَنَّتَيْنِ آتَتْ أُكُلَهَا وَلَمْ تَظْلِم مِّنْهُ شَيْئاًً﴾.
That is, and it did not fall short.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَفَجَّرْنَا خِلالَهُمَا نَهَراً﴾.
So He reported that their watering was from a river, which is the most abundant source of water.

nahhas-meani:34-34.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَكَانَ لَهُ ثُمُرٌ﴾.
It is also read ﴿ثَمَرٌ﴾; «الثَّمَر» (fruit) is well known.
And on «الثُّمُر» there are two views:
a. Mujāhid said: Every «ثُمُر» in the Qurʾān is wealth, and every «ثَمَر» is from fruits.
b. Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī said: «الثُّمُر» is kinds of wealth, and «الثَّمَر» is fruits.
c. Abū Yazīd al-Madanī said: «الثُّمُر» is the stock (the source), and «الثَّمَر» is the fruit.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is as though by "the stock" he means the trees and the like.
These three views come back to one meaning, namely that «الثُّمُر» is wealth.
[Translator's note: the source announces "two views" and then lists three (a–c) before giving "the other view"; translated as written.]
The other view: Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb narrated to us; he said: ʿImrān ibn Bakkār informed me; he said: Ibrāhīm ibn al-ʿAlāʾ al-Zubaydī narrated to us; he said: Shuʿayb ibn Isḥāq narrated to us; he said: Hārūn narrated to us; he said: Abān ibn Taghlib narrated to me from al-Aʿmash that al-Ḥajjāj said: "If I heard anyone say ﴿وَكَانَ لَهُ ثُمُرٌ﴾ I would cut out his tongue." I said to al-Aʿmash: "Do you go by that?" He said: "No, and not the least bit." So he used to read ﴿ثُمُر﴾, taking it as the plural of «ثَمَر».
Abū Jaʿfar said: According to this view the implied derivation is that he pluralised «ثَمَرة» as «ثِمار», then pluralised «ثِمار» as «ثُمْر»; this is good in Arabic. However, the first view is more likely — and Allah knows best — because the saying of the Exalted ﴿كِلْتَا الجنَّتَيْن آتَتْ أُكُلَهَا﴾ indicates that he had fruit.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَقَالَ لَصَاحِبِهِ وَهُوَ يُحَاوِرُهُ﴾, i.e. addressing him, ﴿أَنَا أَكْثَرُ مِنكَ مَالاً وَأَعَزُّ نَفَراً﴾.
[«النَّفَر» is a group of men, fewer than ten; here he means followers, servants and children.]

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَدَخَلَ جَنَّتَهُ وَهُوَ ظَالِمٌ لِّنَفْسِهِ﴾.
And everyone who disbelieves has wronged himself, because he makes it enter the Fire.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿قَالَ مَآ أَظُنُّ أَن تَبِيدَ هَـٰذِهِ أَبَداً. وَمَآ أَظُنُّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ قَائِمَةًً﴾.
So he disbelieved in the Resurrection and in this world's passing away.

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلَئِن رُّدِدتُّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّي لأَجِدَنَّ خَيْراً مِّنْهَا مُنْقَلَباًً﴾.
This is one of the things people ask about, saying: How can he deny the Resurrection and say ﴿وَلَئِن رُّدِدتُّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّي﴾, and decide that he will be given something better than them both?
The answer is that the meaning is: "And if I am returned to my Lord — according to what you say — He has given to me in this world; so just as He gave to me in this world, He will give to me in the Hereafter."
A parallel to this is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَيْنَ شُرَكَائِي﴾? i.e. according to what you say.
And whoever reads ﴿مِنْهَا﴾ means the garden.
[Translator's note: the source raises the question with "better than them both" (منهما) while the verse as quoted reads ﴿مِنْهَا﴾; the remark on «منها» presupposes the variant «منهما». Translated as written.]

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿قَالَ لَهُ صَاحِبُهُ وَهُوَ يُحَاوِرُهُ أَكَفَرْتَ بِٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكَ مِن تُرَابٍ ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍٍ﴾.
So he charged him with unbelief because of his words.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿ثُمَّ سَوَّاكَ رَجُلاً﴾.
That is, He completed you.

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿لَّٰكِنَّاْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ رَبِّي وَلاَ أُشْرِكُ بِرَبِّي أَحَداً﴾.
This indicates that he [the other man] was a polytheist.
The meaning is: «لكِنْ أنا» ("but as for me").

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلَوْلاۤ إِذْ دَخَلْتَ جَنَّتَكَ قُلْتَ مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لاَ قُوَّةَ إِلاَّ بِٱللَّهِ﴾.
The meaning is: [This garden is] what Allah has willed.
And the meaning may be: What Allah wills comes to be.
And the meaning is: Nothing belongs to anyone except what Allah wills, and no one has strength in his body or his wealth except through Allah.
ʿAmr ibn Maymūn related from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Shall I not direct you to a word from the treasure of Paradise, from beneath the Throne?" He said: I said: "Yes indeed, may my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "«لا قوَّةَ إلاَّ باللهِ» (There is no strength except through Allah). When the servant says it, Allah says: My servant has submitted and surrendered."

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إِن تَرَنِ أَنَاْ أَقَلَّ مِنكَ مَالاً وَوَلَداً، فعسَىٰ رَبِّي أَن يُؤْتِيَنِ خَيْراً مِّن جَنَّتِكََ﴾.
He may have meant in this world, or he may have meant in the Hereafter.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَيُرْسِلَ عَلَيْهَا حُسْبَاناً مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ﴾.
Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, a punishment.
Abū ʿUbayda said: They are missiles [the plural of «مرماة», and something containing pelting stones].
What is well known in the language is that «الحُسْبان» and «الحساب» (reckoning) are one, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿الشَّمْسُ وَالقَمَرُ بِحُسْبَانٍ﴾.
And the saying of Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk is sound in meaning; it is as though He said: or send upon it the punishment of the reckoning of what his hands have earned — and it is like the saying of the Exalted ﴿وَاسْأَلِ القَرْيَةَ﴾ [i.e. with a muḍāf omitted].
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَتُصْبِحَ صَعِيداً زَلَقاً﴾.
«الصعيد» in the language is the face of the earth on which there is no vegetation.
And «الزَّلَق» is that on which feet slip.

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أَوْ يُصْبِحَ مَآؤُهَا غَوْراًً﴾.
That is, sunk into the ground; the implied form is «ذا غَوْرٍ» ("having a sinking").
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَلَن تَسْتَطِيعَ لَهُ طَلَباً﴾.
That is, no trace of it remains for which it could be sought.

nahhas-meani:42-42.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَأُحِيطَ بِثَمَرِهِ﴾.
That is, Allah made the punishment encompass his fruit.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿فَأَصْبَحَ يُقَلِّبُ كَفَّيْهِ عَلَى مَآ أَنْفَقَ فِيهَا﴾.
This is how one who regrets is described.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَهِيَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا﴾.
«الخاوية» in the language is "empty", and «العُروش» are roofs.
The meaning is that its walls were standing while its roofs had fallen in, so it was as if the walls were upon the roofs.

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَمْ تَكُن لَّهُ فِئَةٌ يَنصُرُونَهُ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, kinsfolk.

nahhas-meani:44-44.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هُنَالِكَ ٱلْوَلاَيَةُ لِلَّهِ ٱلْحَقِّ﴾.
That is, they believe in Allah alone and disown what they used to worship.
It is also read «الوِلاية» with a kasra on the wāw.
The meaning goes with the fatḥa, because «الوِلاية», as is well known, is governorship (authority).
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿هُوَ خَيْرٌ ثَوَاباً وَخَيْرٌ عُقْباً﴾.
«العُقْب», according to the lexicographers, «العُقْبى» and «العاقبة» are one: it is what a matter ends up as.

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَٱضْرِبْ لَهُم مَّثَلَ ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا كَمَآءٍ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَاءِ فَٱخْتَلَطَ بِهِ نَبَاتُ ٱلأَرْضِ فَأَصْبَحَ هَشِيماًً﴾.
«الهشيم» is what has dried up of clothes [sic] or has crumbled; one says «هشمتُه», i.e. I broke it.
[Translator's note: «الثياب» (clothes) in the source is probably a slip for «النبات» (plants); translated as written.]
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿تَذْرُوهُ ٱلرِّياحُ﴾.
That is, they scatter it.
Allah struck this parable for the life of this world, because what has passed of it is as though it had never been.

nahhas-meani:46-46.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلْبَاقِيَاتُ ٱلصَّالِحَاتُ خَيْرٌ عِندَ رَبِّكَ ثَوَاباً﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū Bakr Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad narrated to us; he said: Qutayba ibn Saʿīd narrated to us; he said: Khālid — he is Ibn ʿAbd Allāh — narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ﴿ٱلْبَاقِيَاتُ ٱلصَّالِحَاتُ﴾ are: (سبحانَ اللهِ، والحمدُ للهِ، ولا إله إلاَّ اللهُ، واللهُ أكبرْ) ("Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is greatest").
And Abū Bakr narrated to us; he said: Qutayba ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Mālik ibn Anas, from ʿUmāra ibn Ṣayyād, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, that he used to say concerning ﴿ٱلْبَاقِيَاتُ ٱلصَّالِحَاتُ﴾ that they are the servant's saying: (سبحانَ اللهِ، واللهُ أكبر، والحمدُ للهِ، ولا إله إلاَّ اللهُ، ولا حول ولا قوة إلاَّ باللهِ) ("Glory be to Allah, Allah is greatest, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, and there is no power and no strength except through Allah").
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is also related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: ﴿ٱلْبَاقِيَاتُ ٱلصَّالِحَاتُ﴾ are "prayer, fasting, pilgrimage, fighting in Allah's path, saying lā ilāha illā Allāh, and glorifying Allah."
None of this is excluded according to the lexicographers, because anything whose reward endures may be called this.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَخَيْرٌ أَمَلاً﴾.
That is, the best of what is hoped for.

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَيَوْمَ نُسَيِّرُ ٱلْجِبَالَ وَتَرَى ٱلأَرْضَ بَارِزَةًً﴾.
On His saying ﴿بارزة﴾ there are two views:
The first: its fruits have been uprooted, its mountains pulled out and its buildings demolished, so it is «بارزة», i.e. exposed.
The exegetes hold this view, and it is the clear one.
The other view: that the meaning of ﴿بَارِزَةً﴾ is that the dead who were in it have been brought out; so this would be by way of nisba (attribution), as [the poet] said: «كِلِيني لِهَمٍّ يَا أُمَيْمةَ نَاصِبِ» ("Leave me, O Umayma, to a wearying care" — i.e. a care that brings weariness).
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَحَشَرْنَاهُمْ فَلَمْ نُغَادِرْ مِنْهُمْ أَحَداً﴾.
That is, We did not leave behind.

nahhas-meani:48-48.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَعُرِضُواْ عَلَىٰ رَبِّكَ صَفَّاًً﴾.
That is, nothing covers them or screens them.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿لَّقَدْ جِئْتُمُونَا كَمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ﴾.
It has been said: Its meaning is: We have raised you as We created you the first time.
And it has been said: It is as is related, that they will be gathered barefoot, [naked] and uncircumcised.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿بَلْ زَعَمْتُمْ أَلَّن نَّجْعَلَ لَكُمْ مَّوْعِداً﴾.
That is, you used to deny the Resurrection.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَوُضِعَ ٱلْكِتَابُُ﴾.
There is an ellipsis (ḥadhf) in the speech; the meaning is: And the book was placed in the hand of every person, either in his right hand or in his left.
Then He made this clear by His saying ﴿فَتَرَى ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ مُشْفِقِينَ مِمَّا فِيهِ وَيَقُولُونَ يٰوَيْلَتَنَا مَالِ هَـٰذَا ٱلْكِتَابِ لاَ يُغَادِرُ صَغِيرَةً وَلاَ كَبِيرَةً إِلاَّ أَحْصَاهَا﴾.
[That is, you see them afraid and fearful of the evil deeds of theirs that are in it, and they say: What is the matter with this book, that it leaves no small or great sin of ours without having preserved and recorded it?]
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَوَجَدُواْ مَا عَمِلُواْ حَاضِراً وَلاَ يَظْلِمُ رَبُّكَ أَحَداً﴾.
That is, the punishment only falls as recompense.
The root meaning of «الظلم» in the language is putting a thing in other than its proper place.

nahhas-meani:50-50.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلاۤئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُواْ لأَدَمََ فَسَجَدُوۤاْ إِلاَّ إِبْلِيسَ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْجِنِِّ﴾.
There are two views on this:
The first: that he was attributed to the jinn because he did their deeds.
The other view: that he was one of them.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَفَسَقَ عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهِ﴾.
That is, he went out.
Al-Farrāʾ reported: «فسَقَتِ الرُّطَبةُ» ("the ripe date has gone out"), when it comes out of its skin.
And Ruʾba said:
يَهْوِينَ في نَجْدٍ وَغَوْراً غَائِراً * فَوَاسِقَاً عَنِ قَصْدهَا جَوَائرَا
(They [the camels] plunge on through highland and deep lowland, straying from their course, swerving aside.)
There is a question about this verse:
It is asked: What is the meaning of ﴿فَفَسَقَ عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهِ﴾?
There are two views on this:
The first — and it is the position of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh — is that the meaning is: fisq (transgression) came to him when he was commanded and disobeyed; so the cause of the transgression was his Lord's command, just as you say: «أطعمتهُ عن جُوعٍ» ("I fed him because of hunger").
The other view — and it is the position of Muḥammad ibn Quṭrub — is that the meaning is: he transgressed by rejecting his Lord's command.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أَفَتَتَّخِذُونَهُ وَذُرِّيَّتَهُ أَوْلِيَآءَ مِن دُونِي وَهُمْ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ﴾? [verse 50].
That is, enemies.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿بِئْسَ لِلظَّالِمِينَ بَدَلاً﴾.
That is, evil is what they took in exchange for obedience to Allah: obedience to Iblīs.

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿مَّآ أَشْهَدتُّهُمْ خَلْقَ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَلاَ خَلْقَ أَنْفُسِهِمْْ﴾.
That is, they did not exist at that time.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَمَا كُنتُ مُتَّخِذَ ٱلْمُضِلِّينَ عَضُداً﴾.
Maʿmar related from Qatāda, who said: helpers.
Abū Jaʿfar said: So it is in the language; one says «عَضَدَني فلانٌ» and «عَاضَدَني», i.e. he helped me and strengthened me.

nahhas-meani:52-52.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَقُولُ نَادُواْ شُرَكَآئِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ فَدَعَوْهُمْ فَلَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُواْ لَهُمْ وَجَعَلْنَا بَيْنَهُم مَّوْبِقاً﴾.
There are several views on its meaning:
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: a place of destruction.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said the same.
Maʿmar related from Qatāda, who said: destruction.
Yazīd ibn Dirham related from Anas ibn Mālik concerning the saying of the Exalted ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا بَيْنَهُم مَّوْبِقاً﴾:
He said: a valley of pus and blood in Hell.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid, who said: a valley in Hell.
Nawf said the same, except that he said: it separates them from the believers.
Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿مَوْبِقَاً﴾: an appointed meeting place.
ʿAwf said: ﴿مَوْبِقاً﴾, i.e. We placed enmity between them.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The soundest of these views is the first, because it is well known in the language that one says «وَبِقَ، يَوْبَقُ، ويَابَقُ، ويَيْبَقُ»,
and «وَبَقَ يَبِق», when someone perishes, and «أوبقه اللهُ», i.e. Allah destroyed him.
From this is: ﴿أَوْ يُوبِقْهُنَّ بِمَا كَسَبُوا﴾.
And from this: «أوبقَتْ فلاناً ذنوبُه» ("his sins destroyed so-and-so").
So the meaning is: We made their mutual ties in this world a place of destruction for them in the Hereafter.
However, it is possible for the valley to be called «مَوْبِق», because it destroys.

nahhas-meani:53-53.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَرَأَى ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ ٱلنَّارَ فَظَنُّوۤاْ أَنَّهُمْ مُّوَاقِعُوهَا﴾.
Maʿmar related from Qatāda, who said: [فظنوا means] they were certain.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلَمْ يَجِدُواْ عَنْهَا مَصْرِفاً﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: That is, a way to turn aside.

nahhas-meani:54-54.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنَا فِي هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنِ لِلنَّاسِ مِن كُلِّ مَثَلٍ وَكَانَ ٱلإِنْسَانُ أَكْثَرَ شَيْءٍ جَدَلاً﴾.
It has been said: By «الإنسان» (man) here the unbelievers are meant, and it has the sense of a group, as the Exalted said: ﴿إنَّ الإِنْسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ. إِلاَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ﴾.
And it has been said: It is general.
In the ḥadīth there is what indicates that it is general: "When the Prophet ﷺ reproached ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib — may Allah be pleased with him — and Fāṭima with him, for not praying at night, ʿAlī said: 'Our souls are in the hand of Allah; when He wills, He releases them.' So the Prophet ﷺ went out saying ﴿وَكَانَ ٱلإِنْسَانُ أَكْثَرَ شَيْءٍ جَدَلاً﴾."

nahhas-meani:55-55.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا مَنَعَ ٱلنَّاسَ أَن يُؤْمِنُوۤاْ إِذْ جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْهُدَىٰ وَيَسْتَغْفِرُواْ رَبَّهُمْ إِلاَّ أَن تَأْتِيَهُمْ سُنَّةُ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ﴾.
There is an ellipsis (ḥadhf) in the speech; the meaning is: except [their] demanding that the way of the former peoples come upon them.
And the way of the former peoples is seeing the punishment with their own eyes, because they said ﴿اللَّهُمَّ إنْ كَانَ هَذَا هُوَ الْحَقَّ مِنْ عِنْدِكَ، فَأَمْطِرْ عَلَيْنَا حِجَارَةً مِنَ السَّمَاءِ، أَو ائْتِنَا بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾, so they demanded the punishment.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أَوْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ [قِبَلاً]﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid, who said: suddenly.
Al-Kisāʾī said: That is, before their eyes.
The two meanings are close.
It is also read ﴿قُبُلاً﴾, and most lexicographers hold that it is the plural of «قَبِيل», i.e. kinds and sorts.
Some of them said: Its meaning is: facing them, as one says «جاءه من قُبُلٍ» ("he came at him from the front").
And the meaning of «قَبِلاً» [sic] is: anew,
as one says: «لا أُكلِّمكَ إلى عَشْرٍ من ذي قِبَلٍ» ("I will not speak to you for ten [days] from now on").

nahhas-meani:58-58.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَل لَّهُم مَّوْعِدٌ لَّن يَجِدُواْ مِن دُونِهِ مَوْئِلاًٍ﴾.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: a refuge.
The lexicographers report «وَأَلَ، يَئِلُ» when someone escapes.

nahhas-meani:59-59.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتِلْكَ ٱلْقُرَىٰ أَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ لَمَّا ظَلَمُواْ﴾.
The meaning is: the people of the towns.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا لِمَهْلِكِهِم مَّوْعِداً﴾.
The meaning may be: for their destruction, in which case it is a maṣdar (verbal noun).
And the meaning may be: for the time of their destruction.
Whoever reads ﴿لِمَهْلَكِهِمْ﴾ takes the meaning to be: for their perishing, as one says «جَلَسَ مَجْلَساً» (he sat a sitting), while the noun of place is «المجلِس»;
and «هَلَكَ مَهْلَكاً», while the noun of place is «المَهْلِك».
Mujāhid said: ﴿مَوْعِدَاً﴾, i.e. an appointed term.

nahhas-meani:60-60.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِفَتَاهُ لاۤ أَبْرَحُ﴾.
It has been said: He was called "his young man" (فتاه) only because he used to serve him, and he was Yūshaʿ (Joshua).
And the meaning of ﴿لاۤ أَبْرَحُ﴾ is "I will not cease", and its meaning is not "I will not move away".
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿حَتَّىٰ أَبْلُغَ مَجْمَعَ ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ﴾.
Maʿmar related from Qatāda, who said: the Sea of the Byzantines and the Sea of Persia.
Someone else said: It is the place at which Allah promised him that he would meet al-Khaḍir.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿أَوْ أَمْضِيَ حُقُباً﴾.
ʿAmr ibn Maymūn related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr: «الحُقْب» is eighty years.
Ibn Najīḥ related, saying: «الحقب» is seventy autumns.
[Translator's note: the source has «ابنُ نجيح» with no further authority named; elsewhere the transmitter is Ibn Abī Najīḥ (from Mujāhid). Translated as written.]
Maʿmar related from Qatāda, who said: «الحُقْب» is a period of time.
Abū Jaʿfar said: What the lexicographers know is that «الحُقْب» and «الحُقْبة» are an indefinite, unlimited stretch of time, just as «قوم» (a people) and «رهط» (a band) are indefinite and unlimited.
And «الحُقُب», with two ḍammas — its plural is «أحْقاب».
And «أحْقاب» may be the plural of «حِقَب», and «حِقَب» the plural of «حِقْبة».

nahhas-meani:61-61.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَلَمَّا بَلَغَا مَجْمَعَ بَيْنِهِمَا﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, between the two seas.
Ubayy ibn Kaʿb — may Allah have mercy on him — said: Ifrīqiya.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿نَسِيَا حُوتَهُمَا فَٱتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُ فِي ٱلْبَحْرِ سَرَباً﴾.
It has been said: Moses' ﷺ forgetting was [his forgetting] to give Yūshaʿ some instruction concerning the fish,
and Yūshaʿ's — peace be upon him — forgetting was [his forgetting] to tell him of its going off through the water.
And it has been said: [to forget] to bring it forward.
Then He said ﴿فَٱتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُ فِي ٱلْبَحْرِ سَرَباً﴾.
«السَّرَب» in the language is the way and the path.

nahhas-meani:64-64.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ ذَلِكَ مَا كُنَّا نَبْغِ﴾.
That is, that which we were seeking, because he had been promised that he would meet al-Khaḍir at the place where it [the fish] slipped away.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَٱرْتَدَّا عَلَىٰ آثَارِهِمَا قَصَصاً﴾.
That is, they went back along the way they had taken, following the tracks closely; «القصص» is following tracks.

nahhas-meani:65-65.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَوَجَدَا عَبْداً مِّنْ عِبَادِنَآ آتَيْنَاهُ رَحْمَةً مِّنْ عِندِنَا وَعَلَّمْنَاهُ مِن لَّدُنَّا عِلْماً﴾.
He means by this al-Khaḍir. It has been said: He was called al-Khaḍir ("the green one") only because whenever he prayed in a place, what was around him turned green.
And in what Moses did — and he was one of the greatest of the prophets and had been given the Torah — in seeking knowledge and travelling for it, there is an indication that no one should give up seeking knowledge, even if he has reached its utmost and comprehended most of what the people of his age can grasp, and that he should be humble towards one who is more knowledgeable than he.

nahhas-meani:66-66.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ لَهُ مُوسَىٰ هَلْ أَتَّبِعُكَ عَلَىٰ أَن تُعَلِّمَنِ مِمَّا عُلِّمْتَ رُشْداًً﴾.
This is the question of one who is gentle, an addresser going to great lengths in good manners. The meaning is: Would it suit you, and be no burden on you, to permit me to accompany you, so that I may take from your knowledge what will guide me? This is as in the ḥadīth: "Can you show me how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to perform ablution?"
«الرَّشَد» and «الرُّشْد» have one meaning, and this is frequent in the Arabic language, as in «البُخْل» and «البَخَل» (miserliness), and «العُرْب» and «العَرَب» (the Arabs).

nahhas-meani:67-67.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ إِنَّكَ لَن تَسْتَطِيعَ مَعِيَ صَبْراً﴾.
This is al-Khaḍir's saying to Moses. Then he told him the reason why he would not be patient, saying: ﴿وَكَيْفَ تَصْبِرُ عَلَى مَا لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِ خُبْرَاً﴾?
That is, how can you be patient with something that appears to be wrong, when you have not been told the wise purpose in it? Prophets do not acquiesce in a wrong, nor is it permissible for them to let it stand; i.e. you cannot keep silent, given your custom and your judgement.

nahhas-meani:69-69.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ سَتَجِدُنِيۤ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ صَابِراًً﴾.
This is Moses' saying to al-Khaḍir, i.e. I will be patient, by Allah's will; ﴿وَلاَ أَعْصِي لَكَ أمْراً﴾, i.e. I have bound myself to obey you, and I will not disobey your command, if Allah wills.

nahhas-meani:70-70.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ فَإِنِ ٱتَّبَعْتَنِي فَلاَ تَسْأَلْني عَن شَيءٍ حَتَّىٰ أُحْدِثَ لَكَ مِنْهُ ذِكْراً﴾.
That is, if you object to it, do not hasten to ask until I explain to you the reason for it, and until I am the one who interprets it for you.
He made it a condition upon him, before the journey began, that he should not ask him or inquire about any of his actions until he disclosed their secret to him; and Moses accepted his condition, observing the etiquette of the learner with the scholar.

nahhas-meani:71-71.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱنْطَلَقَا حَتَّىٰ إِذَا رَكِبَا فِي ٱلسَّفِينَةِ خَرَقَهَا﴾.
Moses and al-Khaḍir set off walking along the seashore until a ship passed by them. They recognised al-Khaḍir and carried them both without fare. When they had boarded the ship, al-Khaḍir took an axe and pulled out one of the ship's planks, after it had reached the open sea. That is the saying of the Exalted ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا رَكِبَا فِي ٱلسَّفِينَةِ خَرَقَهَا﴾, i.e. al-Khaḍir holed it.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ أَخَرَقْتَهَا لِتُغْرِقَ أَهْلَهَا لَقَدْ جِئْتَ شَيْئاً إِمْراً﴾.
That is, Moses said to him, objecting: Have you holed the ship to drown its passengers? You have done a grave and terrible thing.
And the meaning of ﴿إمْرَاً﴾ is: a grave wrong thing.
It is related that when Moses saw that, he took his garment and put it in place of the hole, then said to al-Khaḍir: People who carried us without fare — you went to their ship and holed it to drown its people! You have done a terrible, grave thing.
﴿قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُلْ إِنَّكَ لَنْ تَسْتَطِيعَ مَعِيَ صَبْرَاً﴾! That is, al-Khaḍir said to him: Did I not tell you from the very beginning that you would not be able to be patient with what you see of my doings?!
He reminded him gently of his breaking the condition.

nahhas-meani:73-73.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿ قَالَ لاَ تُؤَاخِذْنِي بِمَا نَسِيتُ وَلاَ تُرْهِقْنِي مِنْ أَمْرِي عُسْراًً﴾.
The meaning of ﴿تُرْهِقْنِي﴾ is "cover me (overwhelm me)", i.e. treat me with ease, not with hardship.
It is related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "The first [objection] from Moses was forgetfulness. And a sparrow came and alighted on the edge of the ship and pecked once in the sea, and al-Khaḍir said to him: My knowledge and your knowledge, compared with the knowledge of Allah the Exalted, are only like what this sparrow has taken away from this sea…"

nahhas-meani:74-74.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱنْطَلَقَا حَتَّىٰ إِذَا لَقِيَا غُلاَماً فَقَتَلَهُ﴾.
That is, he accepted his excuse, and after they had got off the ship they set off walking. They passed by some boys playing, among whom was a boy with a radiant face and handsome appearance. Al-Khaḍir seized him and wrenched off his head with his hand, then threw it on the ground. ﴿قَالَ أَقَتَلْتَ نَفْساً زَكِيَّةً بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ لَّقَدْ جِئْتَ شَيْئاً نُّكْراً﴾, i.e. Moses said to him: Have you killed a pure, innocent soul that never sinned and never killed a soul for which it should be killed?! You have done a grave, abominable thing that cannot be passed over in silence. ﴿قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُلْ لَكَ إنَّكَ لَنْ تَسْتَطِيعَ مَعي صَبْرَاً﴾, i.e. al-Khaḍir said to him: Did I not tell you that you would not be able to be patient with what you see of me? The first time he treated him with deference; then he confronted him with the kāf of address by saying ﴿لك﴾ ("to you"), because there was no excuse here.
The meaning of ﴿زَكِيَّةً﴾ is: innocent, in which nothing requiring its killing was seen.
And here He said ﴿نُكْرَا﴾, i.e. an atrocious wrong, more objectionable than the first matter; it is more emphatic than His saying ﴿إِمْرَاً﴾ in the preceding verse. It is accusative (manṣūb) in two ways:
The first: its meaning is: you have done (أتيتَ) a «نُكْر» thing.
The second: its meaning is: you have come with (جئتَ بـ) a «نُكْر» thing; when the bāʾ was omitted, the verb reached it directly and made it accusative [Translator's note: accusative by removal of the preposition].

nahhas-meani:76-76.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿قَالَ إِن سَأَلْتُكَ عَن شَيْءٍ بَعْدَهَا فَلاَ تُصَاحِبْنِي قَدْ بَلَغْتَ مِن لَّدُنِّي عُذْراً﴾.
That is, if I object to you after this time and challenge what comes from you, do not keep me in your company; you have given me fair warning and alerted me to my breaking of the condition, so you are excused in my eyes.

nahhas-meani:77-77.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱنطَلَقَا حَتَّىٰ إِذَآ أَتَيَآ أَهْلَ قَرْيَةٍ ٱسْتَطْعَمَآ أَهْلَهَا﴾.
That is, they walked until they reached a town and asked for food, but they did not give them any; they asked them for hospitality, but they did not host them.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: It is Antioch.
Ibn Sīrīn said: It is al-Ayla.
Then the Exalted said: ﴿فَوَجَدَا فِيهَا جِدَاراً يُرِيدُ أَن يَنقَضَّ فَأَقَامَهُ﴾.
The meaning is: they found in the town a leaning wall about to fall down and collapse, so al-Khaḍir passed his hand over it and it stood straight.
And it has been said: He demolished it and then rebuilt it.
It is related that Moses said to al-Khaḍir: People from whom we asked food did not feed us, and we sought their hospitality and they did not host us, and then you sit down to build the wall for them! ﴿لَوْ شِئْتَ لَتَّخَذْتَ عَلَيْهِ أَجْراً.﴾.
* And the saying of the Exalted ﴿يُرِيدُ أَن يَنقَضَّ﴾ means: it was about to fall. This is majāz (figurative usage) and extension of meaning, and it is frequent in the speech of the Arabs and their poetry. Of this is the saying of ʿAntara:
وَازْوَرَّ مِنْ وَقْعِ القَنَا بَلَبَانِهِ * وَشَكا إليَّ بِعَبْرةٍ وَتَحَمْحُم
(And he [my horse] swerved from the blows of the spears on his breast, and complained to me with a tear and a whinny.)
And the saying of another:
يُرِيدُ الرُّمْحُ صَدْرَ أبي بَرَاءٍ * ويَرْغَبُ عَنْ دِمَاءِ بَنِي عَقِيَل
(The spear "wants" the breast of Abū Barāʾ, and "shuns" the blood of Banū ʿAqīl.)

nahhas-meani:78-78.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ هَـٰذَا فِرَاقُ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنِكََ﴾.
Sībawayh holds that repeating «بين» in a case like this is for tawkīd (emphasis), i.e. "the parting between us", just as one says «أخزَى اللهُ الكاذبَ مني ومنك» ("May Allah disgrace the liar, of me and of you"), i.e. of us.

nahhas-meani:79-79.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمَّا ٱلسَّفِينَةُ فَكَانَتْ لِمَسَاكِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ فِي ٱلْبَحْرِ﴾.
The lexicographers all — we know of no disagreement among them — say: «المسكين» is one who has nothing, and «الفقير» is one who has a little something.
Most of the jurists hold the opposite of this regarding the two, and they cite this verse as proof.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It has been said: His saying ﴿كَانَتْ لِمَسَاكِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ فِي البَحْرِ﴾ does not indicate that they owned it. Do you not see that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever sells a slave who has property, his property belongs to the seller"?
So his saying "who has property" (له مال) does not entail that he owns it. This is very frequent; of it is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنَّ أَوْهَنَ البُيُوتِ لَبَيْتُ العَنْكَبُوتِ﴾.
And of it is their saying "the door of the house" and "the saddle-cloth of the riding beast": things are annexed to things without that entailing ownership. So it [the ship] was annexed to them because they worked on it, just as the property was annexed to the slave because it is with him.
And the derivation requires what the lexicographers said, because «مسكين» is taken from «السكون» (stillness), which is absence of movement, so it is as though he were in the position of a dead man.
And «الفقير» is as though his vertebrae (فَقار) had been broken, so some remnant still remains to him.
This is also indicated by the ḥadīth of the Prophet ﷺ: Aḥmad ibn Manṣūr al-Ḥāsib narrated to us; he said: ʿAlī ibn al-Jaʿd narrated to us; he said: Ḥammād ibn Salama informed us, from Muḥammad ibn Ziyād, who said: I heard Abū Hurayra say: I heard Abū al-Qāsim, peace be upon him, say: "The miskīn is not the one who goes round [begging] and is sent away with a date or two, or a mouthful or two; rather, the miskīn is the one who does not find sufficiency to suffice him, and does not beg from people importunately."
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَانَ وَرَآءَهُم مَّلِكٌ يَأْخُذُ كُلَّ سَفِينَةٍ غَصْباً﴾.
Ibn ʿUyayna related from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read ﴿وَكَانَ أَمَامَهُمْ مَلِكٌ﴾ ("and there was before them a king").
Abū Jaʿfar said: On «وراء» here there are two views:
The first: that it has the sense of «أمام» (in front).
The other: that it has the sense of «خلف» (behind), in its basic meaning, as though He said: on their way when they return.
The first view is better, because Ibn ʿAbbās — may Allah have mercy on him — read accordingly, and because the language permits it: whatever is hidden from you is «وراء», so this applies to what is in front.
Then He said ﴿يَأْخُذُ كُلَّ سَفِينَةٍ غَصْباً﴾.
And ʿUthmān — may Allah have mercy on him — read ﴿كُلَّ سَفِينَةٍ صَالِحَةٍ غَصْبَاً﴾ ("every sound ship by force").

nahhas-meani:80-80.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَأَمَّا ٱلْغُلاَمُ فَكَانَ أَبَوَاهُ مُؤْمِنَيْنِ﴾.
Ibn ʿUyayna related from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read ﴿وَكَانَ أَبَوَاهُ مُؤْمِنَيْنِ وَكَانَ كَافِرَاً﴾ ("and his parents were believers, and he was an unbeliever").
And Ubayy ibn Kaʿb related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "He was stamped with unbelief, and love of him was cast upon his parents."
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَخَشِينَآ أَن يُرْهِقَهُمَا طُغْيَاناً وَكُفْراً﴾.
﴿فَخَشِينَا أَنْ يُرْهِقَهُمَا﴾.
﴿فَأَرَدْنَا أَنْ يُبدَلهُمَا﴾.
Abū Ḥātim said: This is from the speech of Moses' companion, meaning al-Khaḍir.
Someone else said: It is from the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
If someone says: How can ﴿فَخَشيِنَا﴾ ("We feared") be a report about Allah?
The answer to that is that al-Farrāʾ said ﴿فَخَشِينَا﴾ has the sense of "We knew", just as one says «ظنَنَّا» ("we supposed") in the sense of "we knew".
The Basrans said: One says «خشيتُ الشيءَ» in the sense of "I disliked it" and in the sense of "I was alarmed by it", as a man says: "I fear (أخشى) that such-and-such may be", i.e. I dislike [it].
Al-Akhfash said: In the reading of Ubayy: ﴿فَخَافَ رَبُّكَ أَنْ يُرْهِقَهُمَا طُغْيَانَاً وَكُفْرَاً﴾ ("so your Lord feared that he would burden them…").
Someone else said: And so it is in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd].
The discussion of «خِفْتُ» and «خَشِيتُ» is the same.
Al-Akhfash reported «خفتُ أن تقولا» in the sense of "I disliked that you two should say".
And the meaning of ﴿أَنْ يُرْهِقَهُمَا﴾ is: that he would bring upon them, i.e. drive them into «الرَّهَق», which is ignorance (folly).
Abū Zayd said: «أرهقتُه» means "I burdened him".

nahhas-meani:81-81.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَرَدْنَآ أَن يُبْدِلَهُمَا رَبُّهُمَا خَيْراً مِّنْهُ زَكَـاةً وَأَقْرَبَ رُحْماًً﴾.
Ibn Jurayj said: ﴿زَكَاةً﴾, i.e. Islam.
Al-Farrāʾ said: righteousness.
Ibn Jurayj said: And ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym narrated to me from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: They were given a girl in exchange for him.
Ibn Jurayj said: And they were more compassionate towards her.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: They were given a girl in exchange for him, and she gave birth to a prophet.
Al-Farrāʾ reported: «رحِمتُه رَحْمَةً، ورُحْمَةً» (I had mercy on him — two maṣdar forms).
Al-Aṣmaʿī reported from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ: «رَحِمَهُ اللهُ رُحْمَاً».
And according to the school of al-Khalīl, «رَحْماً» with a fatḥa is permissible.

nahhas-meani:82-82.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلْجِدَارُ فَكَانَ لِغُلاَمَيْنِ يَتِيمَيْنِ فِي ٱلْمَدِينَةِ وَكَانَ تَحْتَهُ كَنزٌ لَّهُمَا﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Mujāhid said: knowledge.
Qatāda and ʿIkrima said: wealth.
This view is preferable from the standpoint of language, because when it is said "So-and-so has a treasure (كنز)", what is meant is only buried, stored wealth.
If something else is intended, it is made explicit, and one says: he has a treasure of knowledge, a treasure of understanding.
And it may be as is related, that it was a tablet of gold on which was written "There is no god but Allah; Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah"; this combines wealth and knowledge.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا فَعَلْتُهُ عَنْ أَمْرِي ذَلِكَ تَأْوِيلُ مَا لَمْ تَسْطِـع عَّلَيْهِ صَبْراً﴾
indicates that this was by revelation.

nahhas-meani:83-83.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَن ذِي ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ قُلْ سَأَتْلُواْ عَلَيْكُم مِّنْهُ ذِكْراً﴾.
Abū al-Ṭufayl related that Ibn al-Kawwāʾ asked ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib — may Allah be pleased with him — about Dhū al-Qarnayn: was he a prophet or a king? He said: "He was neither a prophet nor a king, but a righteous servant who loved Allah, so He loved him, and was sincere to Allah, so Allah was sincere to him. He was struck on his right horn (side of the head) and died, and Allah raised him; then he was struck on his left horn and died. And among you there is one like him."
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the most eminent chain of transmission related concerning his being named Dhū al-Qarnayn ("the one with two horns").
It has also been said: He had two braids.
And it has been said: Because he reached the two extremities of the earth, the East and the West.
Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq said: One who transmits the reports of the non-Arabs, concerning what they inherited of knowledge about him, told me: Dhū al-Qarnayn was a man of the people of Egypt, named Marzubān ibn Mardaba the Greek, a descendant of Yūnān son of Yāfith son of Noah.
Ibn Hishām said: His name was al-Iskandar (Alexander), and he is the one who built Alexandria, so it was named after him.
Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq said: And Thawr ibn Yazīd narrated to me, from Khālid ibn Maʿdān al-Kalāʿī — and he was a man who had met [the people of the earlier generation] — that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about Dhū al-Qarnayn and said: "A king who surveyed the earth from beneath it by means (bi-l-asbāb)."
Khālid said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb — Allah's mercy be upon him — heard a man say: "O Dhū al-Qarnayn!" and ʿUmar said: "O Allah, forgive! Are you not content to name yourselves after the prophets, until you name yourselves after the angels?"

nahhas-meani:84-84.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّا مَكَّنَّا لَهُ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَآتَيْنَاهُ مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ سَبَباً﴾.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: knowledge.
The meaning according to this interpretation is: knowledge by which he could manage to travel through the regions of the earth.

nahhas-meani:85-85.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿فَأَتْبَعَ سَبَباً﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid, who said: a stopping place and a route between the East and the West.

nahhas-meani:86-86.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا بَلَغَ مَغْرِبَ ٱلشَّمْسِ وَجَدَهَا تَغْرُبُ فِي عَيْنٍ حَمِئَةٍ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and Ibn al-Zubayr read ﴿حَامِية﴾ ("hot").
Ibn ʿAbbās read ﴿حَمِئَةٍ﴾ ("muddy").
Abū Jaʿfar said: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿArafa narrated to us; he said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us; he said: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us; he said: ʿAmr ibn Maymūn narrated to us; he said: I heard Abū Ḥāḍir say: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: I was with Muʿāwiya, and he recited ﴿تَغْرُبُ فِي عَيْنٍ حَامِيَةٍ﴾. I said: We only read it «حَمِئَة». He said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr: "How do you read it, O ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr?" He said: "As you read it, O Commander of the Faithful." I said: "It was in my house, O Commander of the Faithful, that the Qurʾān was sent down."
So Muʿāwiya sent for Kaʿb and said: "Where do you find the sun setting in the Torah?" He said: "As for Arabic, you know it better; as for me, I find in the Torah the sun setting in water and mud," and he pointed with his hand towards the West. [Abū Ḥāḍir said:] I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: "Had I been with you, I would have supported you with a word by which you would gain more insight into «حَمِئَة»." Ibn ʿAbbās said: "What is it?" I said: "In what we transmit of the saying of Tubbaʿ, in which he made mention of Dhū al-Qarnayn, in his words:
بَلَغَ المَشَارِقَ وَالْمَغَـارِبَ يَبْتَغِي * أَسْبَابَ أَمْرٍ من حَكيمٍ مُرشِدِ
(He reached the places of sunrise and sunset, seeking the means of a command from a Wise One who guides.)
فَرَأىَ مَغِيبَ الشَّمْسِ عندَ غُروبِهَا * في عَيْن ذِيِ خُلْبٍ، وثأَطٍ حَرْمَدِ
(And he saw where the sun goes down at its setting, in a spring of clay and black mire.)"
Ibn ʿAbbās said: "What is «الخُلُب»?" He said: "Clay, in their speech." He said: "And what is «الثَّأْط»?" I said: "Black mud (الحَمْأة)." He said: "And what is «الحرمد»?" I said: "Black."
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the explanation of «الحَمْأة». One says «حمئتِ البئر» when black mud has come into the well; «أَحْمأتُها» — I threw black mud into it; and «حمَّأْتُها» — I took the black mud out of it.
As for the reading of whoever reads ﴿حامية﴾, it can bear two meanings:
The first: that the meaning is «حَمِئَة», as though he said «حامئة», i.e. having black mud, and then the hamza was lightened.
The other meaning: that it has the sense of "hot".
And it may be hot while also having black mud; and Allah knows best its reality.
Al-Qutabī [Ibn Qutayba] said: This spring may be part of the sea, and the sun may set behind it, or with it, or at it, the preposition being put in the place of another; and Allah knows best about that.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَوَجَدَ عِندَهَا قَوْماً قُلْنَا يٰذَا ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ إِمَّآ أَن تُعَذِّبَ وَإِمَّآ أَن تَتَّخِذَ فِيهِمْ حُسْناً﴾.
Ibrāhīm ibn al-Sarī [al-Zajjāj] said: He gave him the choice between these two, just as He gave Muḥammad ﷺ the choice, saying: ﴿فَإِنْ جَاءُوْكَ فَاحْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ أَوْ أَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ﴾.
ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān [al-Akhfash the Younger] said: The meaning is: We said, O Muḥammad, they said: O Dhū al-Qarnayn.

nahhas-meani:87-87.t:
He said: Because after it comes ﴿قَالَ أَمَّا مَن ظَلَمَ فَسَوْفَ نُعَذِّبُهُ ثُمَّ يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِ فَيُعَذِّبُهُ عَذَاباً نُّكْراً﴾.
So how could he say to his Lord ﴿ثُمَّ يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِ﴾? And how could he say ﴿فَسَوْفَ نُعَذِّبُهُ﴾? A servant does not address [his Lord] in this way. And it is not established that Dhū al-Qarnayn was a prophet, such that Allah would say ﴿قُلْنَا يَا ذَا الْقَرْنَيْنِ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a difficult passage; the omission of «القول» (the verb of saying) is not impossible, and Allah knows best what He intended.
Maʿmar related from Qatāda concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿فَسَوْفَ نُعَذِّبُهُ﴾, that he said: by killing.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِ فَيُعَذِّبُهُ عَذَاباً نُّكْراً﴾,
because the punishment of the Hereafter is more terrible than killing.

nahhas-meani:88-88.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَأَمَّا مَنْ آمَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحاً فَلَهُ جَزَآءً ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ﴾.
It has been said: «الحسنى» here is Paradise.
It is also read ﴿فَلَهُ جَزَاءُ الحُسْنَى﴾, i.e. [the reward of] good-doing.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَسَنَقُولُ لَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِنَا يُسْراً﴾.
That is, a kindly word.

nahhas-meani:89-89.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ اتَّبَعَ سَبَباًً﴾.
It is also read ﴿ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَ﴾ with a disjunctive alif (hamzat al-qaṭʿ), i.e. one of the means that would bring him to the regions of the earth.
Al-Aṣmaʿī said: One says «أتبعتُ القومَ», with a disjunctive alif, meaning I caught up with them;
and «اتَّبعتهم», with a conjunctive alif (hamzat al-waṣl), when you passed along in their tracks even if you did not catch up with them.

nahhas-meani:90-90.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا بَلَغَ مَطْلِعَ ٱلشَّمْسِ وَجَدَهَا تَطْلُعُ عَلَىٰ قَوْمٍ لَّمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُمْ مِّن دُونِهَا سِتْراً﴾.
That is, they had no buildings and no shirts.
Al-Ḥasan said: When it rose, they went down into the water until it set.
As for the meaning of ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾, it has been said about it: their ruling is like the ruling of those upon whom the sun sets, i.e. they are like those.

nahhas-meani:93-93.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَ سَبَباً حَتَّىٰ إِذَا بَلَغَ بَيْنَ السَّدَّيْنِ﴾.
It is also read ﴿السُّدَّينِ﴾.
Abū ʿAmr and a group of the lexicographers distinguished between the two.
Some of them said: «السُّدّ» is what is of Allah's making, and «السَّدّ» (with fatḥa) is what is of human making.
And it has been said: «السَّدّ» is what you see, and «السُّدّ» is what screens your eyes.
What is correct in this is what al-Kisāʾī said: that they are two dialectal forms with one meaning.
And if one were to add something to this, it would be said: «السَّدّ» is the maṣdar (verbal noun), and «السُّدّ» is the noun.

nahhas-meani:94-94.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُواْ يٰذَا ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ إِنَّ يَأْجُوجَ وَمَأْجُوجَ مُفْسِدُونَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ فَهَلْ نَجْعَلُ لَكَ خَرْجاً عَلَىٰ أَن تَجْعَلَ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَهُمْ سَدّاً﴾.
It is also read ﴿خَرَاجَاً﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ said: «الخَرْج» is the maṣdar (verbal noun), and «الخَراج» is the noun.
Maʿmar related from Qatāda on ﴿خَرْجَاً﴾ that he said: a gift (payment).
And so it is in the language; one says «لك عندي خَرْجٌ», i.e. a gift and a fee. And «الخَراج» is the familiar [word, i.e. land-tax], even though its origin is from this.

nahhas-meani:95-95.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ مَا مَكَّنِّي فِيهِ رَبِّي خَيْرٌٌ﴾.
That is, better than what you have offered me.
And «الرَّدْم» in the language is more than «السَّدّ» (a barrier), because it is something dense, layered one part on another.
ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī related from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿بَيْنَ السُدَّينِ﴾ — the two mountains: Armenia and Azerbaijan.

nahhas-meani:96-96.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿آتُونِي زُبَرَ ٱلْحَدِيدِ﴾.
«الزُّبَر» are large pieces of iron.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا سَاوَىٰ بَيْنَ ٱلصَّدَفَيْنِ﴾
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: the two mountains.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ ٱنفُخُواْ حَتَّىٰ إِذَا جَعَلَهُ نَاراً﴾.
It has been said: He laid down the pieces of iron, placed firewood and charcoal between them and lit a fire on them; and iron, when a fire is lit on it, becomes like fire. That is His saying ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا جَعَلَهُ نَاراً﴾.
Then he melted brass and poured it over it; that is the saying of the Exalted ﴿قَالَ آتُونِيۤ أُفْرِغْ عَلَيْهِ قِطْراً﴾,
i.e. give me molten metal (قِطْر) that I may pour over it.
And whoever reads ﴿ائْتُوني﴾, the meaning for him is: Come, that I may pour copper over it.

nahhas-meani:97-97.t:
He, Exalted be His name, said: ﴿فَمَا ٱسْطَاعُوۤاْ أَن يَظْهَرُوهُُ﴾.
That is, to climb over it, because of its height and smoothness.
One says «ظهرتُ على السطح», i.e. I climbed up onto the roof.
Kaʿb said: They work at it every day, and when evening comes they say: "Tomorrow we will break through it," and they are not granted to say "if Allah wills". Then, when Allah permits their coming out, they say "if Allah wills", and they break through it and come out. The first of them drink up the Tigris and the Euphrates, so that when the last of them passes by he says: "There was once water here." The people of the earth are harmed by them, and Jesus — Allah bless him and grant him peace — invokes [Allah] against them, and they perish.

nahhas-meani:98-98.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ هَـٰذَا رَحْمَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّي﴾.
[That is, this empowerment is a mercy from my Lord.]
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعْدُ رَبِّي جَعَلَهُ دَكَّآءَ﴾.
That is, level with the ground.
One says «ناقةٌ دكَّاءُ», i.e. a she-camel that has no hump.

nahhas-meani:99-99.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتَرَكْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَمُوجُ فِي بَعْضٍ﴾.
By ﴿يَوْمِئذٍ﴾ ("on that day") the day they come out from the barrier may be meant,
or the Day of Resurrection may be meant, because of the saying of the Exalted ﴿وَنُفِخَ فِي ٱلصُّورِ فَجَمَعْنَاهُمْ جَمْعاً﴾.

nahhas-meani:102-102.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَفَحَسِبَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوۤاْ أَن يَتَّخِذُواْ عِبَادِي مِن دُونِيۤ أَوْلِيَآءَ﴾.
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: The meaning is: Do those who disbelieve reckon that it will benefit them to take My servants as patrons besides Me?
ʿAbbād ibn al-Rabīʿ related that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib — Allah's mercy be upon him — read: ﴿أَفَحْسَبُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنْ يَتَّخِذُوا عِبَادِي مِنْ دُوْنِي أَوْلِيَاءَ﴾ ("Is it then sufficient for those who disbelieve that they take My servants…").
Abū ʿUbayda said: That is, are they content with that? Does that suffice them?
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إِنَّآ أَعْتَدْنَا جَهَنَّمَ لِلْكَافِرِينَ نُزُلاً﴾.
«النُّزُل» according to the lexicographers is what is prepared for the guest and the like; and «النَّزَل», with two fatḥas, is yield (increase).

nahhas-meani:104-104.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿قُلْ هَلْ نُنَبِّئُكُم بِٱلأَخْسَرِينَ أَعْمَالاً. ٱلَّذِينَ ضَلَّ سَعْيُهُمْ فِي ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَهُمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ يُحْسِنُونَ صُنْعاً﴾.
Abū al-Ṭufayl related that ʿAlī said: They are the first of [the people of] Ḥarūrāʾ.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays related from ʿAlī, who said: They are the monks.
Al-Aswad said: Joy and jesting were seen in ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, so Ibn al-Kawwāʾ al-Yashkurī stood up and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, who are those whose effort has gone astray in the life of this world? Are they the Ḥarūriyya?" He said: "No; they are the People of the Book. Their first ones were upon the truth; then they disbelieved and associated partners [with Allah]."
Shuʿba related from ʿAmr ibn Murra, from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd, who said: I said to Saʿd: "Who are those whose effort has gone astray in the life of this world? Are they the Khawārij?" He said: "They are the Jews and the Christians. As for the Jews, they did not believe in Muḥammad; and as for the Christians, they did not believe in the Resurrection [as it truly is], because they said there is no eating or drinking in Paradise. So their effort went astray and their deeds came to nothing, while they reckoned they were rightly guided: ﴿أُوْلَئِكَ الَّذِيْنَ كَفَرُوْا بِآيَاتِ رَبِّهِمْ وَلِقَائِهِ﴾.
As for the Khawārij, they are those about whom Allah said: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَنْقُضُونَ عَهْدَ اللَّهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ مِيثَاقِهِ، وَيَقْطَعُونَ ما أَمَرَ اللهُ بهِ أَنْ يُوصَلَ﴾."
[Translator's note: the bracketed "as it truly is" is added for clarity; the source has simply «فلم يؤمنوا بالقيامة».]

nahhas-meani:105-105.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَلاَ نُقِيمُ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ وَزْناً﴾.
Abū Hurayra related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "On the Day of Resurrection the huge, tall man, the great eater and drinker, will be brought, and he will not weigh [even] the wing of a gnat. Recite, if you wish: ﴿فَلاَ نُقِيمُ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ وَزْناً﴾."

nahhas-meani:107-107.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ كَانَتْ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتُ ٱلْفِرْدَوْسِ نُزُلاً﴾.
Abū Umāma was asked about al-Firdaws, and he said: It is the navel (the very centre) of Paradise.
Kaʿb said: It is the one in which there are grapevines.
Abū Isḥāq said: «الفردوس» is the garden that gathers everything that is found in gardens, and so it is according to the lexicographers. We have not heard it [in Arabic poetry] except in a verse of Ḥassān:
وإنَّ ثَوَابَ اللَّهِ كُلًّ مُوَحِّدٍ * جِنَانٌ مِنَ الفِرْدَوسِ فِيهَا يُخَلَّدُ
(Allah's reward for every believer in His oneness is gardens of al-Firdaws, in which he will abide forever.)
It was read before Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Firyābī, from Qutayba ibn Saʿīd, who said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: "In Paradise there are a hundred degrees; between every two degrees is [the distance] between heaven and earth. Al-Firdaws is the highest [part] of Paradise; above it is the Throne of the All-Merciful, and from it the rivers of Paradise gush forth. So when you ask Allah, ask Him for al-Firdaws."

nahhas-meani:108-108.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا لاَ يَبْغُونَ عَنْهَا حِوَلاً﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid, who said: a moving away.
Someone else said: It is from «الحيلة» (stratagem), i.e. they do not contrive to get to anything else.

nahhas-meani:109-109.t:
And His saying, exalted be His mention: ﴿قُل لَّوْ كَانَ ٱلْبَحْرُ مِدَاداً لِّكَلِمَاتِ رَبِّي لَنَفِدَ ٱلْبَحْرُ قَبْلَ أَن تَنفَدَ كَلِمَاتُ رَبِّي﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means knowledge.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَلَوْ جِئْنَا بِمِثْلِهِ مَدَداً﴾.
It has been said: ﴿مَدَدَاً﴾ has the sense of «مِداداً» (ink).
And it has been said: It is from their saying «نحنُ مَدَدٌ له» ("we are a reinforcement for him").
And Ibn ʿAbbās read: ﴿وَلَوْ جِئْنَا بِمِثْلِهِ مِدَاداً﴾.

nahhas-meani:110-110.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَمَن كَانَ يَرْجُواْ لِقَآءَ رَبِّهِ﴾.
It has been said: ﴿يرجو﴾ has the sense of "fears", as the poet said:
إِذَا لسَعَتْهُ النَّحْلُ لَمْ يَرْجُ لَسْعَهَا * وَحَالفَهَا في بَيْتِ نُوْبٍ عَوَامِلِ
(When the bees sting him he does not fear their sting, and he keeps close to them in the hive of busy, swarming bees.)
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: ﴿لِقَاءَ رَبِّهِ﴾, i.e. the reward of his Lord.
Abū Jaʿfar said: On this [view] ﴿يرجو﴾ is in its basic sense ("hopes"); and when he hopes for his Lord's reward, he fears His punishment.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ يُشْرِكْ بِعِبَادَةِ رَبِّهِ أَحَدَاً﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means showing off.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: That is, he does not show off.
Kathīr ibn Ziyād said: I asked al-Ḥasan about His saying ﴿فَمَن كَانَ يَرْجُواْ لِقَآءَ رَبِّهِ فَلْيَعْمَلْ عَمَلاً صَالِحاً﴾: concerning whom was it revealed? He said: "It was revealed concerning the believer." I said: "Can he be a polytheist?" He said: "He associates [others] in the deed, when he does a deed intending by it Allah and people; and that is what is thrown back at him."
